clue.text: Be taking pains to get to the seaside?

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the seaside is the place of sandy shores

blocks.note: taken as written
pains are aches

explanation.surface: Someone goes to great trouble to reach the coast for a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking pains' reads as making an effort, but here it simply supplies a word for pains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy or pebbly shores where people holiday make up what Britons call a trip to the coast.

clue.text: Chopper turned up with colliery to inspect

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: an axe is a chopping tool
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A helicopter flies over a coal pit to look it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but it is the tool used for chopping wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look at it closely and carefully, which is what inspecting means.

clue.text: Animal arrived and left

blocks.note: arrived means came
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A creature turns up and then goes away again.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is a humped desert beast, a specific example of the general category named.

clue.text: Divorcee with more than enough for a case

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A divorced person has plenty of money to bring a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds legal after 'Divorcee', but it means an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is one instance illustrating a point, just as a case is a single occurrence cited.

clue.text: Seems to have inserted article in different papers

indicators.note: a different version of the word that follows means its letters are rearranged
something inserted is put inside another word, here the reworked one

blocks.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor notes that a piece of writing has been slipped into various newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe giving an impression, so 'she appears tired' and 'she seems tired' say the same thing.

clue.text: Twisted pastel parts of flower

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so the following word loses its order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pale-coloured blooms have curled at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Petals are the coloured leaf-like sections around the centre of a bloom.

clue.text: Administrator having about four put to death

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: to put to death is to execute
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A manager orders the execution of four people.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for 'put to death' wraps around the Roman numeral for four, sitting just before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager who runs an organisation, a person who administers its affairs.

clue.text: Turned man out of famous gallery

indicators.note: the man sits out of, meaning outside, the gallery, so he surrounds it

blocks.note: Rod is a man's name
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A man was thrown out of a well-known art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' reads as expulsion, but it places the name Rod around the gallery's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated is a past tense verb meaning spun round on an axis, just as turned can mean.

clue.text: Goody-goody Simon can't produce promises to pay

indicators.note: to produce from these letters is to make something new out of them by rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A prim man named Simon is unable to come up with promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctimonious person makes a show of moral superiority, which is the self-righteous goody-goody adjective.

clue.text: Special Sunday when friend gets married

definitions.note: the answer names the Sunday, as in Palm Sunday

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A friend's wedding day falls on a memorable Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Palm Sunday is the Sunday before Easter, marking Jesus's entry into Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Sunday is the particular church festival day before Easter, so the first word of its name identifies it.

clue.text: Accommodation for separated people on backstreet

indicators.note: back attached to the street word asks for that word read the other way round

blocks.note: separated means apart
men are people
St is the abbreviation for street; the word fuses the reversal signal with the street

explanation.surface: Flats are provided in a side road for couples who have split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like one word for a side road, but it splits into a reversal signal and the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartments are flats or sets of rooms where people live, a form of lodging or housing.

clue.text: Rejected tablet, if it's something adding stimulation

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the following words are read backwards

blocks.note: a tablet is a pill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a pill, unless it gives a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus that livens something up, an encouraging lift.

clue.text: City where California needs to reduce volunteers

blocks.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
to reduce is to cut
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A state facing budget pressures must trim its volunteer workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: Calcutta, now Kolkata, is a major Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcutta is the former official name of Kolkata, the large Indian metropolis in West Bengal.

clue.text: Agree mine should be moved into a zoo

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted around into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that their own pets ought to be rehoused in a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for display, essentially a small zoo.

clue.text: Tear out data on works of art

indicators.note: a word put out of joint is disordered, so its letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
data are facts

explanation.surface: A researcher rips out the information about paintings and sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Artefacts are objects made by human hands, often of cultural interest, so crafted pieces fit.

clue.text: Find some Gershwin dynamic, but pompous

indicators.note: finding some of the following words means taking a run of letters from inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A critic finds part of a Gershwin piece lively yet overblown.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy in its informal sense means long-winded and full of empty talk, as a self-important speaker is.

clue.text: Catches sight of pimples

blocks.note: first meaning: notices or sees
second meaning: blemishes on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone notices acne in the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for noticing something and a plural noun for small skin blemishes.

clue.text: Study of pro-life doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A report examines a physician opposed to abortion.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a short descriptive article about a person, a written study of them.

clue.text: They get together to get things moving

definitions.text: They get together to get things moving

blocks.clueFragment: They get together to get things moving
blocks.note: surface reading: people meeting to make progress on a plan
setter's reading: toothed wheels mesh with each other to drive machinery

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a committee starting a project; 'get together' really means interlock, as gears do.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed wheels in a mechanism engage one another, transmitting motion and setting machines in operation.

clue.text: Film we take back on board

blocks.note: taken as written
the stern is the rear of a ship, the back when on board

explanation.surface: A group returns to a ship to see a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a cowboy movie set in the American frontier, one genre of cinema.

clue.text: They have to put up with other people

definitions.text: They have to put up with other people

blocks.clueFragment: They have to put up with other people
blocks.note: surface reading: people forced to tolerate others
setter's reading: be housed alongside other people as paying guests

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' suggests tolerance, but it means being given a room in someone else's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying tenants who rent a room in a householder's house are given board there among the family.

clue.text: Beefy SRN got drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written; a State Registered Nurse in old British usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burly nurse became intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy describes a muscular, powerful build, which is a synonym for physically mighty.

clue.text: It may be aimed at people leaving the church

definitions.text: It may be aimed at people leaving the church

blocks.clueFragment: It may be aimed at people leaving the church
blocks.note: surface reading: criticism directed at people abandoning their faith
setter's reading: a newly married couple walking out after the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a rebuke to lapsed worshippers, but the people are newlyweds being showered as they exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper scraps thrown over a bride and groom after a wedding ceremony are traditionally tossed at the couple.

clue.text: Joiner coy about getting a drink

indicators.note: one word going about another surrounds it like a fence

blocks.note: coy means shy
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: A bashful carpenter goes off to fetch something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is a joining word. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a British pub beverage of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Are holding back, if intensely passionate

indicators.note: held back here means the little word is turned the other way round
a word holding another has it inside, clasped between its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are restraining yourself while burning with feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire literally means burning, and figuratively describes someone ablaze with strong emotion or ardour.

clue.text: Terrible cold is sure to produce leak

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful mess, so the words that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad head cold is certain to give someone a runny nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' and 'leak' suggest a streaming nose, but the leak is of information.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is an unauthorised revelation of secret information, which is a kind of disclosure.

clue.text: I live with a cross and horny creature

blocks.note: taken as written
to live is to be, to exist
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone shares a home with an angry, lustful beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' tempts a racy reading, but it simply means having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long, curved, ridged horns.

clue.text: Meaning jam takes a long time?

blocks.note: a jam is a mess, a tricky situation
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone complains that making preserves is slow work.
explanation.definitionFit: The message of a speech or story is its underlying point or significance.

clue.text: Anger greatly, smoking in church?

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to make furious
second meaning: aromatic burning material used in worship

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at a person lighting up during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: the 'smoking' is fragrant fumes rising during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enrage; as a noun it is fragrant resin burnt to make smoke in religious rites.
